deviations: tupleLiteral now refuses a nested literal, returning null, which the gates report as a reshaped tuple. The spec text says the first closing bracket ends the list so nesting hides members; refusing it is stricter than the spec, and it closes the same hole comments opened.

The tuple's facet-order check holds facet order only (topics, then skills, then languages). Order within a facet is free, as the tag-tuple format asks. The spec's reference page, not the tuple, uses tag-list order within a facet.

Naming any of the tags gate's own data files (docs/data/tags.json, site/src/lib/types.ts, docs/data/allow/tags.json) makes the run whole, including the dead-member and allowlist checks. The earlier comment said named paths never widen a run.

The shared stamp matcher (lib/generated.ts FILE_STAMP) also accepts MDX's {/* … */} form, which the site lane's hubs use (output-ownership-C2: any comment syntax). This widens check-claims too, harmlessly, since it reads only .md files.
